english.title: Owner / keeper of equine fail to arrange implantation of transponder / replacement transponder
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..) being the

(A)_[owner having primary day-to-day responsibility for an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), that was deemed to be identified in accordance with Articles 4(2) or 43(1) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/262,]_
(B)_[keeper of an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), that was deemed to be identified in accordance with Articles 4(2) or 43(1) of the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/262 and for which the owner did not have primary day-to-day responsibility,]_

failed to arrange, for the purposes of Article 18(5) of that Regulation, for a veterinary surgeon to implant a transponder into that equine when

(C)_[a previously implanted and recorded transponder had ceased to function]_
(D)_[the equine arrived in England having been subject to an alternative method of identity verification authorised by another member State under Article 21]_
(E)_[the equine had not already had a transponder implanted in compliance with the requirements or specifications as to transponders set out in the EU Regulation or Commission Regulation (EC) No 504/2008 of 6 June 2008 implementing Council Directives 90/426/EEC and 90/427/EEC as regards methods for the identification of equidae; and was born on or before 30th June 2009]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 13(2), 24 and 36 of the Equine Identification (England) Regulations 2018.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
owner/keeper of equine
failed to arrange for vet to implant transponder into equine
that has been previously implanted and recorded but now cease to function OR
the equine arrives into the UK having been subject to an alternative method of identity verification authorised by another member EU state

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 37(1) provides that an enforcing authority may impose a civil sanction, or a combination of civil sanctions, under Part 6 against a person if the authority is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the person is guilty of this offence.
(ii) Regulation 37(2) provides that criminal proceedings may not be started or continued against a person if any enforcing authority, in respect of the offence, chooses to apply civil sanctions and services a compliance notice, non-compliance penalty notice or fixed monetary penalty notice on that person.

SUMMARY: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 monthsNote
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
